Overview

What is TYB

Tokyo Youth Battle is a 4,444-piece collection on Robinhood Chain. It isn't just a mint — every piece is also a ticket in a live gacha with on-chain payouts, its traits can evolve, there's a friendlier guaranteed way in for Frog Heads holders, and a refund window if you change your mind.

Ways in

Four ways in

The mint opens in phases, in this order: GTD → FCFS → Frenzy → Public. Each phase is one-way — once it moves on, it doesn't go back. GTD and FCFS share a 2 per-wallet cap; from Frenzy on it rises to 6.

1 · GTD — guaranteed

Burn a Frog Heads NFT before mint to lock a guaranteed allowlist spot — no gas wars, no gatekeeping. Mint up to 2 here (shared with FCFS).

2 · FCFS — allowlist

A first-come, first-served allowlist. If you're on the list you can mint before it opens to everyone — within the same 2 per-wallet cap as GTD.

3 · Frenzy

The cap opens up: your per-wallet limit rises to 6. If you already minted 2 in GTD/FCFS, you can mint 4 more here.

4 · Public

Open to anyone, up to 6 per wallet, while supply lasts.

GTD via Frog Heads burn

Holding Frog Heads earns you a guaranteed spot. Before mint opens you burn a Frog Heads NFT (on Ethereum); the burn is recorded on-chain, snapshotted, and turned into the guaranteed allowlist. When the GTD phase opens, burners mint their guaranteed pieces.

  • The burn is irreversible — once burned, that Frog Heads is gone.
  • Up to 2 Frog Heads per wallet count toward GTD (one guaranteed mint each).
  • Burn window and the exact snapshot cutoff are announced before mint. dates TBD
The gacha

The gacha mechanic

Every TYB is a numbered ticket (its token ID). Each round opens with its winning numbers public. Buy a ticket ($0.50 each, up to 20 per transaction) and your number shows instantly — every ticket pays straight to the holder (not the dev) of the number it draws, and the first ticket to hit a winning number takes the prize. The dev takes no cut of the payouts — every cent of every ticket flows to holders, and the entire prize goes to the winner. The round runs on a committed random seed, revealed at close so anyone can verify everything on-chain, including that nothing is skimmed.

⚠️

When the gacha starts depends on the mint. Part of the mint proceeds seed the gacha prize pool — so the first round begins once the mint has performed well enough to fund it.

⚠️

Hold to earn. Each ticket's payout goes to whoever holds the drawn number's NFT when the round settles — not the ticket buyer, and not an earlier holder. Sell your TYB before a round settles and the new owner receives that payout. TYB rewards holders: hold through the round to receive what your number earns.

  • Beyond the chance at the prize, every ticket also earns you a power-up — an on-chain item you keep for a future use. to be announced
  • Prizes, per-ticket payouts and any refunds are pooled into one balance you claim on the Claim page.
  • Round price, cadence and prize details are published per round. round params TBD
Evolution

Trait evolution

Every gacha ticket also earns you a power-up — one of 5 trait categories, at random. Power-ups are their own on-chain items; you claim them next to your ETH on the Claim page. Burn one to try to evolve that trait on one of your TYB, from the Inventory.

  • Traits have three tiers. Evolving Tier 1 → Tier 2 succeeds 1/10 of the time; Tier 2 → Tier 3 is 1/20. Tier 3 is the top.
  • The power-up is spent whether the roll passes or fails — the odds are the odds.
  • Each trait's level lives on-chain (anyone can verify it), and the roll can't be predicted or gamed when you commit. On a pass, your piece's art and metadata update.
To be announced
Refund & royalties

85% refund window

Changed your mind? During the refund window after mint you can burn your TYB and reclaim 85% of the mint price back to your wallet — no questions.

  • Only the original minter who still holds the piece can refund. If it was sold or transferred, the refund is disabled.
  • It's a blind refund — it happens before the art reveal.
  • Refund returns 0.0017 ETH per piece (85% of 0.002 ETH).

Royalties

Secondary sales carry a 5% royalty (ERC-2981), enforced on-chain (ERC721-C) and honored by marketplaces like OpenSea.

FAQ

Frequently asked

Why don't Frog Heads holders get a free mint?

Frog Heads was itself a free mint — a second free mint on top would just dilute what holders already earned. Instead, a holder converts a Frog Head into a guaranteed (GTD) spot by burning it, which also removes Frog Heads supply. It's a trade, not a giveaway.

What's the point of burning Frog Heads and dropping a new collection?

Two things: it brings new people into the ecosystem, and it adds value to Frog Heads by burning supply — every burn permanently removes one, making the rest scarcer.

Do I need Frog Heads to mint?

No. Frog Heads gives you a guaranteed spot via the burn, but FCFS and public phases are open to others.

Is the gacha "pay to win"?

The prize is funded by the house, and every ticket's value flows to holders — a holder-first mechanic, verifiable on-chain after each round's reveal. Bought after a round was already won? You get a full refund.

Can I max out a trait?

You can try. Power-ups drop at random and the roll is honest odds, so maxing a specific trait takes a bit of luck — life isn't fair, and that's part of it.

What if I don't like my piece?

Burn it during the refund window for an 85% refund (original minter only) — the window is before the reveal, so it's a blind refund while every piece still shows the placeholder.

When does the art reveal?

After the refund window closes. Until then every piece shows the placeholder.

Any plans for the royalties?

Yes. With Frog Heads we've put the ETH from royalties into buybacks and burns — over 600 NFTs burned that way so far. We want to do the same with TYB, add more prizes and go further: using the royalties to expand the TYB IP if the project does well.
